key_highlights: ASX rises on Wall Street's best day in six weeks; big four banks advance, oil and bond yields ease (21, 43)
RBA chief flags inflation concerns; IMF urges spending cuts as another rate hike looms (21, 57)
Houthi attacks threaten Saudi oil supply, spiking global crude and diesel prices (1, 30, 52)
Iron ore sentiment deteriorating; 'roaches seethe' signals weak demand outlook (23)
Japan lifts rates to counter 'shocking' inflation, pressuring AUD and global risk assets (7)
Recession odds for 2027 rising; housing 'absurdly unaffordable' (16, 31)
Anthropic lands $31bn datacentre deal in western Queensland, boosting tech/infrastructure (74)
Multiple WA exploration wins: Dalaroo Cu-Ni-PGE, Jupiter rare earths, Augustus gold (46, 48, 49)
Coles maintains elevated milk prices despite axing farmer support; consumer cost pressure persists (41)
Victoria backs away from renewable transmission projects, complicating energy transition (28)

sectors.trend: Iron ore sentiment weak with 'roaches seethe' commentary; however, WA exploration wins (Dalaroo Cu-Ni-PGE, Jupiter rare earths, Augustus gold) provide selective upside. Gold discovery by Aurum in Côte d'Ivoire adds to precious metals narrative.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face headwinds from soft iron ore demand. Junior explorers (Dalaroo, Jupiter/Critica, Augustus) offer speculative upside. Gold miners benefit from safe-haven flows amid Middle East tension.

sectors.trend: Big four banks advance on the day; however, soaring state interest costs and IMF spending-cut warnings pressure sovereign credit and lending volumes. RBA inflation worry implies further rate hikes ahead.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from wider NIMs if RBA hikes, but credit risk rises with recession odds climbing. State government debt servicing (55) pressures fiscal spending and infrastructure pipeline.

sectors.trend: Houthi attacks threaten Saudi oil, spiking crude and diesel to record $6/gallon. Japan diverts Australian LNG to its own market, starving East Coast supply. Victoria retreats from renewable transmission. Coal policy under political pressure.
sectors.implications: Woodside (WDS.AX), Santos (STO.AX) benefit from LNG price spikes but face export diversion risk. Coal names (WES.AX, BRL.AX) face policy uncertainty. Petrol price shock (30) pressures transport and consumer sectors.

sectors.trend: Coles holds milk prices high despite removing farmer support; SA government injects $109m into struggling wine industry. Cue and Veronika Maine face collapse. Petrol shock adds to cost-of-living pressure.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, CBA.AX (retail lending) face margin pressure. Wine sector (e.g., Treasury Wine Estates TWE.AX) gets state support. Consumer discretionary names under pressure from affordability crisis.

sectors.trend: Housing 'absurdly unaffordable'; tenants finally see relief. ACCC moves to break real estate agency monopoly. Rising interest costs hit state budgets and housing supply.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) face mixed signals: tenant relief may ease vacancy but rate hikes pressure valuations. ACCC action (58) could reshape agency fee structures, benefiting property managers.

sectors.trend: Anthropic secures $31bn datacentre in western Queensland. AI regulation proposals (rogue incident reporting). Oracle layoffs signal global tech consolidation.
sectors.implications: Datacentre build-out benefits construction (WTC.AX, CGP.AX) and power infrastructure. AI regulation may slow adoption but create compliance opportunities. CSL.AX and healthcare tech remain defensive anchors.

RBA rate hike cycle vs. rising 2027 recession probability
Iron ore demand weakness vs. WA exploration upside
Consumer affordability crisis: petrol, milk, housing
Japan rate hike and global monetary divergence
State government fiscal stress from soaring interest costs
Energy transition policy inconsistency (Victoria renewables retreat, coal policy)

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Middle East oil supply disruption (Houthi attacks)
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge energy exposure; monitor Brent crude and AUD/USD; favour domestic energy producers (WDS.AX, STO.AX) over importers
Reduce leverage; favour dividend-paying defensives (CSL.AX, WES.AX); monitor unemployment and retail sales data
Underweight BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX; rotate into gold and critical minerals (Jupiter, Dalaroo)

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Japan rate hike / global monetary divergence
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor AUD/USD; Japanese outflows may pressure global risk assets; hedge FX exposure
Avoid state-linked infrastructure contracts; monitor sovereign credit ratings
Favour essential-staple defensives; avoid discretionary consumer exposure

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight domestic energy producers on oil/LNG price spike
opportunities.rationale: Houthi attacks and Japan LNG diversion support crude and gas prices; WDS and STO benefit from higher realisations

opportunities.recommendation: Selective exposure to WA critical minerals and gold explorers
opportunities.rationale: Dalaroo Cu-Ni-PGE, Jupiter rare earths, Augustus gold, and Aurum Côte d'Ivoire discovery offer asymmetric upside amid iron ore weakness
Anthropic $31bn QLD datacentre drives construction, power, and telecom demand over 3–5 years

opportunities.recommendation: Defensive dividend rotation into healthcare and staples
opportunities.rationale: Recession risk and rate hikes favour low-beta, high-dividend names; CSL and WES provide income and stability

defensive_moves.rationale: Deteriorating iron ore demand outlook; China slowdown risk; 'roaches seethe' signals structural weakness
Japan rate hike, RBA inflation worry, and IMF spending-cut pressure create headwinds for AUD and rate-sensitive sectors
Affordability crisis, petrol shock, and rising rates pressure discretionary spending and property valuations

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to consolidate near recent highs on oil-driven energy strength and bank outperformance, but RBA inflation commentary and Japan rate hike cap upside. Volatility elevated on Middle East headlines. 1–3 month range-bound with sector rotation from materials to energy/defensives.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautious: rising 2027 recession odds, IMF fiscal warnings, and iron ore demand weakness weigh on growth. However, AI infrastructure capex (Anthropic), critical minerals transition, and domestic energy security provide structural tailwinds. Expect a choppy, dividend-led market with selective mining/tech upside.
